# Course assignments

Student owns access and progress for Courses assigned to each student. An
assignment references the ordinary `course_id` owned by `ms-go-course`; there
is no additional structure identity between Course and its Modules.

A student may have several assignments at the same time. The database enforces
uniqueness only for `(student_id, course_id)`, not for `student_id` alone.
Assignment states are `ASSIGNED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PAUSED`, `COMPLETED`, and
`ARCHIVED`. The default student list hides archived rows.

Learning Planner assigns a Course through:

- `PUT /internal/students/{studentID}/courses/{courseID}/assignment`;
- body `planning_request_id` and `assigned_by=learning_planner`;
- UUID `Idempotency-Key` header;
- dedicated `LEARNING_PLANNER_INTERNAL_TOKEN`.

The general internal token is not accepted by this route. The assignment and
its command receipt commit in one PostgreSQL transaction. Replaying the same
key and body returns success without creating another row; reusing a key or a
planning request for another command returns `409`.

After assignment, Learning Planner replaces the student's current Learning
Path through the same dedicated-token contour. The route uses optimistic
versioning and authoritative lesson IDs/targets returned by Course. Assignment
and path replacement are separate idempotent commands: retry repairs a partial
failure without granting Planner ownership of Student progress or mastery.

Students read only their own non-archived assignments through:

- `GET /api/v1/student/courses`;
- `GET /api/v1/student/courses/{courseID}`.

Course title, outline, and lifecycle remain Course-owned and are not copied
into the assignment row.

An exact non-archived assignment also authorizes the authenticated student to
read a Course whose Course-owned `catalog_visible` flag is false. Student first
uses the ordinary public Course preflight. Only after that fails may it read
trusted metadata and verify the returned `course_id` against its own assignment;
missing, foreign, and archived assignments remain inaccessible.
